title: Owner can set fee to 100% and capture all swap proceeds
root_cause: Treasury.setFeeBps() lets the owner set the fee up to 10000 bps; at 100% the owner captures all swap output.
attacker_entrypoint: Treasury.setFeeBps(10000) — but this is onlyOwner; only the trusted owner can call it.

severity_justification.worst_case: Owner sets fee to 100% and captures all swap proceeds.
severity_justification.realistic_case: Requires the trusted owner to act maliciously; this is a privileged/admin action, not an external attack.
severity_justification.program_table_mapping: Would be High if privileged actions were in scope — they are not for this program.

call_trace: user -> Treasury.swap(): feeBps applied, owner receives 100% of output
asset_delta: Up to 100% of swap output redirected to the owner.
reproduction_steps: Assert a user swap routes 100% of output to the owner
false_positive_risks: This is privileged owner behaviour, typically considered an accepted trust assumption.
invalidating_conditions: Requires the owner key; not reachable by an unprivileged attacker.

defense_analysis.why_it_fails: It does not fail — onlyOwner correctly restricts the call to the trusted owner, which is exactly why this is privileged-only.
No max-fee cap exists, but the action still requires the owner role.

assumptions: Requires the owner to be malicious or compromised.
triager_summary: Exploit requires the admin/owner role, which the program does not accept as in scope. Privileged-only; must not be submitted.
